observations: REPORTING-YEAR OFFSET: file year = CDP submission year; each response reports the prior calendar year (2016 file -> 2015 data, 2017 -> 2016, 2018 -> 2017, 2019 -> 2018, 2020 -> 2019).

FACILITY DEFINITION: W5 "facilities" are mostly river-basin/catchment groupings of many sites (e.g. Limpopo WMA = 26 sites in 2016, 15 in 2017, 16 in 2018, 7 in 2019), so group membership changes year to year; only Los Bronces (2015, 2018-2019), Minas-Rio, Quellaveco, Victor, Unki are single sites. Site names in this file carry the catchment label; see record notes for constituents.

GROUPING CHANGES: Los Bronces was its own facility in 2015 (basin "Salado"), merged into the Aconcagua group in 2016-2017 (36,374 and 34,968 ML), and split out again under "Maipo" from 2018. Sishen/Kolomela were in the Orange WMA group in 2015 and in the Vaal group from 2016. Namibia group basin labelled "Orange" in 2015 and "South Atlantic Coast" later; De Beers Canada labelled "St. Lawrence" in 2015.

METHODOLOGY BREAK 2017: from reporting year 2017 Anglo American aligned with ICMM water accounting; group withdrawals jumped from 226,509 ML (2016) to 306,275 ML (2017) while described as "about the same"; groundwater 83,098 -> 139,176 ML; Victor facility 3,020 -> 32,907 ML. 2015-2016 values are not comparable with 2017+.

SCOPE CHANGE 2018: Namdeb and Debswana (non-managed JVs) excluded from the 2018 boundary; they were ~20% of 2017 withdrawals, 21% of discharges, 99% of seawater withdrawal (seawater 33,935 -> 15 ML). New Vaal, New Denmark, Kriel divested Feb 2018.

RESTATEMENT: the 2017 response says 2016 discharge (136,039 ML) was 3% lower than RESTATED 2015 discharge; originally reported 2015 discharge was 110,937 ML, implying a material upward restatement (~140,000 ML) that is not disclosed numerically.

CONSUMPTION DEFINITION: 2015 consumption (222,866 ML; 221,000 ML in W8.1a of the same file) far exceeds withdrawals minus discharge (137,536 ML) - it appears to be "new water consumption" incl. other definitions. From 2017 onwards consumption = withdrawals minus discharge (company acknowledges this is not a true ICMM consumption figure).

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES (facility level): 2016 data - Aconcagua (36,374) and Minas-Rio (17,251) consumption equal their withdrawals despite 248 and 13,900 ML discharged; Limpopo consumption 34,804 > withdrawal 34,260. 2015 data - several facilities have consumption > withdrawal (e.g. Debswana 25,221 vs 19,317; Limpopo 37,655 vs 37,041). 2019 data - Mackenzie facility consumption -358 ML (discharge > withdrawal). 2019 Los Bronces labelled "Much higher" although withdrawals fell 24,879 -> 16,703 ML.

RECYCLING RATE: 2015 stated as 69% (W1.1) and 64% (W8.1b) in same file; 2016 66%; 2017 ~60% (estimated); 2018 ~70%; 2019 ~70%. Company notes recycled data partly estimated because many sites lacked water balances (only 60% of sites had completed/restated water balances at end-2018). 2020 response gives "% of target achieved" 80 while text says 93%.

TARGET EVOLUTION: 2016 file - reduce consumption 14% (29,995 ML) vs 2020 BAU forecast 192,272 ML (set 2011; 16% saving achieved by 2015). 2017 file - target reset to 19% (20,595 ML) vs BAU 108,393 ML on 7 material sites, 2015 baseline (22,865 ML avoided in 2016); recycling goal changed from 80% (no date) to 75% by 2020; new goal -20% absolute freshwater intake by 2020. 2018 file - WETT replaced by Sustainable Mining Plan: 75% recycling by 2020, -20% freshwater intake by 2020 (2015 baseline), >85% recycling by 2030, -50% freshwater abstraction in water-scarce regions by 2030, no Level 3+ incidents by 2020.

TARGET PROGRESS REGRESSION: freshwater intake reduction vs 2015 reported as 13% in both the 2018 and 2019 responses (identical, possibly not updated), then 7% in the 2020 response (RY2019) - i.e. 35% of the 2020 target and 14% of the 2030 goal; company states improved water accounting puts 2020 milestones at risk and baseline will be reset in 2020 with ICMM definitions.

WATER STRESS EXPOSURE: share of operations/mines in water-stressed/high-risk areas stated as >70% (2016 file), ~75% (2017 file), 50% (2018, 2019 files), "over 50%" (2020 file). Share of withdrawals from stressed areas: 55% (2017), 58% (2018), 51-75% range "higher" (2019). All 13 facilities flagged as in water-stressed areas in 2019 except the two Canadian ones.

LOS BRONCES DROUGHT (key physical risk): 2015 - 6th consecutive dry year, ~18,000 t copper lost, ~$90.5m loss; 2017 - flooding of pit/haul roads after wet 2016-17, 2 weeks lost production, $53m; 2019 - driest year of decade-long mega-drought, production -9% to 335,000 t (2018: 369,500 t), $207m lost revenue (34,500 t x $6,000/t). Response spend: $180m recycling system (2016 file), $74m (2017 file), $70m (2018 file), $20m (2019 file), $17m (2020 file). Evaporation covers piloted (up to 85-90% evaporation reduction); CPR potential saving ~$18m/yr; evaporation-loss saving ~$15m/yr (site uses ~30 million m3/yr new fresh water at ~$2/m3).

MINAS-RIO: Peixe river supplies up to 80% of fresh water; abstraction halted Sept-Oct 2015, 16 Jul-15 Nov 2016, 24 Jul-1 Nov 2017 (regional scarcity permit limits; tailings-dam reserve nearly exhausted in 2017). March 2018 slurry pipeline leaks (318 t and 174 t into Santo Antonio stream) -> 280 days suspension, $0.6bn EBITDA impact, fines $32.4m + $17.5m (total $50m, 11 fines). One-day lost production valued at $3.8m (2018 file), $0.9m (2019 file), $6.3m (2020 file).

MOGALAKWENA / LIMPOPO: value of one day of lost production $3.3m (2018 file, revenue $1.2bn), $3.6m (2019 file, $1.3bn), $4.1m (2020 file, $1.5bn). $6m Polokwane sewage works upgrade for +6 ML/day (spent $3.8m by 2017, $5.2m by 2018, $6.7m since 2014 by 2019); treated effluent allocation raised to 20 ML/day in 2019. Regional Limpopo water balance: region extremely water stressed until beyond 2028; significant supply shortfalls expected 2022; province severely stressed 2022-2025.

OTHER RISK FIGURES: eMalahleni water reclamation plant (treats up to 50 ML/day) capex $1.5bn cited as Olifants risk magnitude (2018-2020 files). Canada (Snap Lake, Trend, Victor) water management cost ~$100m/yr (2016-2018 files) but $10m/yr in 2019 file; Trend Se treatment potential $100m (2018 file) vs $10m (2019 file). Los Bronces Donoso acid drainage: ~$30m collection system spent; treatment plant $60m (2017-2018 files) revised to $35m (2019-2020 files), only needed 2020-2022. El Soldado sulphate seepage: potential fine $6m, $1m drains. Group-wide pipeline asset review $10m after 823 m3 Los Bronces release (2017). $440m spent on a water supply project in Peru (2018 file, W7.1). Substantive-impact threshold: >$25m.

FINES/INCIDENTS: 2015 one enforcement order (Minas-Rio, $0); 2016 two Minas-Rio fines ($32,375 and $274,445); 2017 no water fines reported; 2018 11 fines $50m (Minas-Rio); 2019 2 administrative fines $54,000 (Brazil, contested). Level 3 environmental incidents: 14 (2014), 6 (2015), 4 (2016), 2 (2017), 5 + one Level 4 (2018, stricter classification), 1 (2019). Coal SA had two mine-water overflow incidents at Khwezela/Landau in 2016 (Kopseer, Schoongezicht dams).

CAPEX/OPEX TRENDS (estimated % change in water-related spend): 2015 capex +13%/opex -4% (Platinum & Kumba only); 2016 +24%/+27%; 2017 +10%/+10% (forward capex +500%); 2018 -50%/-50% (forward +50%/+10%); 2019 +10%/+10% (forward capex +100%). Company states it has no clear definition of water capex. >$10m invested to close gaps vs new water standard (2018 file).

CLIMATE/FORESIGHT: climate vulnerability studies (Imperial College, UK Met Office, CSIR) rank Chile and Peru as highest-risk; Mogalakwena modelling predicts ~10% increase in high/low rainfall margins, shorter wetter rainy periods, longer dry periods; Platinum SA statistical climate signal expected beyond 2048; company cites predicted 40% global water shortfall by 2030. Waterless-mine ambition: dry processing/CPR expected to allow 80% process-water reuse and 30-40% less water per unit of production.

DATA QUALITY: water withdrawals and consumption externally verified (76-100% of facilities; ISAE 3000 cited in the 2017 response) in the 2016 and 2017 responses, but "Not verified" for all aspects in the 2018 response; 2019-2020 responses repeatedly state data "has not been verified or validated against the water balance".

COMMUNITY WATER SPEND: $1.72m community water & sanitation projects in 2015; $5.3m CSI water & sanitation in 2016; Mogalakwena supplied ~35,000 residents in 12 villages by bowser (2015); Mapela community water project targeting 70,000 people (45,000 connected by 2018).

FACILITY vs GROUP TOTALS: sum of W5 facility withdrawals is below group total each year (2015: 246,598 vs 248,473; 2016: 226,340 vs 226,509; 2017: 296,887 vs 306,275; 2018: 217,288 vs 227,497; 2019: 208,989 vs 209,868 ML) - group totals include offices, exploration, labs, Element Six, Vergelegen etc. Sum of 2015 facility discharges (102,498) is well below the 110,937 group total.

PRODUCTION VALUE fields in W4.1c (e.g. Limpopo 28,483,061 in 2018 file; stated as tonnes milled/processed in 2019-2020 files) were not extracted as ore_processed_t because the unit is only implied and basins are aggregated.
